solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rear several deer on outskirts of city zone

indicators.note: the deer word sits around the zone word, forming its outer edges

parts.note: hinds are female deer, and several of them make a plural
a quarter is a district of a city, like the Latin Quarter

explanation.surface: A herd of deer rears up on the fringes of an urban district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a verb about deer rearing up, but it is the noun meaning the back end of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hind parts of an animal are its rear, so the two are synonyms for the back end.

clue.text: Most divine fiction given coverage in Mass

indicators.note: the fiction word is covered by, so sits within, the Mass word

parts.note: the host is the consecrated bread of the Mass
a lie is an untruth, a fiction

explanation.surface: The most sacred tale is reported on during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The holiest thing is the most sacred, the superlative of holy, matching most divine.

clue.text: Nth herring lost at sea, a must-see for Arctic cruisers?

indicators.note: something at sea is confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A herring lost in the far north is something every polar cruise passenger wants to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nth' looks like an abbreviation for North but is just fodder letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora borealis is a natural light show in polar skies, a prime attraction on Arctic voyages.

clue.text: Scruple from catering officer holding up army lunch's starters

indicators.note: the officer's letters hold the picked letters between them

parts.note: a quartermaster, QM, handles army supplies including food

indicators.note: the starters of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A mess officer has misgivings about delaying the troops' lunch starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like a first course, but picks the initials U, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualm is a pang of conscience or doubt, the same as a scruple.

clue.text: Like a sloth carried into middle of sea

indicators.note: the carried word goes into the centre of the sea's name

parts.note: the Aral Sea is in Central Asia
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: A sloth is carried into the middle of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloths live in trees, and arboreal means tree-dwelling.

clue.text: Two sailors on vacation have a restless night, perhaps

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied of its contents, leaving just its outer letters

explanation.surface: A pair of sailors on holiday sleep badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties both words: TWO gives TO and SAILORS gives SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss, as in toss and turn, is to move about fitfully in bed, one sign of a bad night.

clue.text: Square one circle at random

indicators.note: putting letters in a random order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: squaring one circle by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' and 'circle' evoke squaring the circle; 'Square' here is the verb meaning settle.
explanation.definitionFit: To square accounts or differences is to settle them, bringing them into agreement.

clue.text: Upset at a politician's money-raising strategy

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at an MP's fundraising plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalisation is how a firm funds itself, through shares and borrowing, its scheme for raising money.

clue.text: Remained sober on air

indicators.note: speech broadcast on air is heard rather than seen, so it signals a sound-alike

parts.note: staid means serious and sober in manner

explanation.surface: A broadcaster stayed sober while live on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained in a place, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Iberian writer, fifty or thereabouts

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ca, short for circa, means approximately

explanation.surface: A Spanish author is described as being about fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or thereabouts' reads as one phrase of approximation, but 'or' is taken as written and 'thereabouts' alone gives CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a celebrated Spanish poet and playwright, Spain being on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: Backwoodsman uses this road and sea transport, stabling horse

indicators.note: to stable a horse is to house it, so the transport words take the horse letter in

parts.note: road transport here is a bus, the road vehicle
a craft is a boat or ship
H is slang shorthand for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A wilderness dweller travels by bus and boat while keeping a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: H is put between BUS and CRAFT. 'Horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushcraft is the set of outdoor survival skills a person living in the wild relies upon.

clue.text: They won't last long: record time on edge

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A record whose time is running out is teetering on the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things enjoyed or used only briefly, such as tickets or flyers, transient by nature.

clue.text: Dishevelled Eastern ducks released close to boundary

indicators.note: to duck is to dodge out of the way, so the Eastern letter leaves

parts.note: untied means freed from a knot or tether

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Scruffy birds from the East are set free near a fence line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like birds, but is a verb: E ducks out of UNTIED, leaving UNTID, then Y ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untidy in appearance is unkempt or messy, a plain synonym for being dishevelled.

clue.text: Like ring a designer included in collection, after reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so the whole build reads backwards
the article and designer go inside the collection word

parts.note: a lot is a batch of items at auction
Christian Dior was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A designer's ring is included in a jewellery collection, seen in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a doughnut-shaped ring, so toroidal describes something shaped like a ring.

clue.text: Hypocritical trendy church about to admit offence

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the offence goes inside

parts.note: in means fashionable
CE is the Church of England
re means concerning, about
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: A fashionable church is two-faced about confessing wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' means let in: the offence is let into the middle of the trendy-church-about run, not at its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An insincere person says what they do not mean, which is the essence of being a hypocrite.

clue.text: Hotshot from Ritz regularly put in charge

indicators.note: the picked letters are placed inside the word for charge

parts.note: a ward is a person in someone's charge or care

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the hotel's name, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A high-flyer from the Ritz hotel is regularly given responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is an expert, someone brilliantly skilled, just as a hotshot is.

clue.text: Hypothetical element in current trade talk

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a deal is a trade or transaction
gas is idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: A theoretical component is found in today's trade discussions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day' but gives physics' I for current.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal gas is a theoretical model of a gas, imagined substance used in physics.

clue.text: Sleepers finally resent abuse

parts.note: sleepers are spies planted long in advance, like moles

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word resent

explanation.surface: Sleeper agents eventually come to resent mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleepers' looks like people asleep or railway sleepers; in spy jargon both sleepers and moles are long-term undercover agents.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest is to harass or abuse someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Overcoming irritability, doctor's on the move

indicators.note: in a down clue the doctor coming over another word sits above it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
bile is bad temper, from the humour once thought to cause it

explanation.surface: Having got over a bad temper, a doctor is now up and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile means able to move about freely, so someone mobile is on the move.

clue.text: In the midst of a commotion, grand lady's holding fast

indicators.note: the lady goes into the middle of the commotion phrase

parts.note: a din is a loud noise or uproar
her is a pronoun for a woman
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Amid an uproar, a stately woman clings on tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand lady' reads as one grande dame, but 'grand' supplies its own letter at the very end, and 'lady' alone goes into the commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhering means sticking firmly to something, the same as holding fast.

clue.text: There's European support for island nation short of a missile

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so the European letter comes after
the island nation's name lacks the article letter

parts.note: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation

explanation.surface: Europe backs a small island nation lacking a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, a kind of projectile or missile.

clue.text: Previous drink knocked back, getting extra round

indicators.note: the extra word goes around the reversed drink

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket

indicators.note: knocking a drink back sounds like gulping it, but here the drink word is turned backwards

parts.note: nog is a strong ale or eggnog

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink and gets an extra round of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' makes GON from NOG. A bye is a run scored in cricket without the batter hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Bygone means belonging to the past, a synonym for previous or former.

clue.text: Exotic plant explorer found on island

indicators.note: in an across clue the explorer placed on the island comes after it

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan navigator and explorer

explanation.surface: A traveller discovers a strange plant while on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a Mediterranean plant of legend, its forked root said to shriek when pulled up.

clue.text: Competitor in pool runs down in motor

indicators.note: in a down entry, the runs letter shifts lower, further along the word

parts.note: to motor is to drive
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A competitor knocks someone down while driving.
explanation.walkthrough: R moves from second place to the end of DRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver competes in a swimming pool, plunging from boards or platforms.

clue.text: River flowing through the Broads

indicators.note: the river runs across the words, so its letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: A river runs through the Norfolk Broads.
explanation.walkthrough: The Broads are a network of waterways in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river in northern Spain, flowing into the Mediterranean.

clue.text: One likely to drop stretcher and fly?

parts.note: a litter is a stretcher for carrying the sick or injured
a fly is an insect, loosely a bug

explanation.surface: Someone may drop a stretcher and run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests a stretcher-bearer losing grip; the definition means dropping rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug is a person who carelessly throws rubbish on the ground in public places.

clue.text: The French see fuel in tank reduced by a third

indicators.note: the fuel word goes inside the shortened tank
one of the three letters of the tank word is cut off

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: French people look at fuel in a tank that is only two-thirds full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by a third' drops the final letter T of the three-letter tank word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French exclamation means literally 'see there', used when presenting something.

clue.text: Troubled OR man's recent petition

indicators.note: troubled letters are stirred up and disordered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried man from operating theatres files a recent petition.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the operating room; 'Troubled' rearranges OR MANS RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a formal protest or complaint, often presented as a petition to authority.
